info.name: Lost and Found City Network API
info.description:
Backend API for the City-wide Lost and Found Network.

Quick Start:
1. Run: docker-compose up -d
2. Register or Login — tokens are saved automatically as collection variables.
3. All other requests use Bearer auth via the accessToken variable.

Swagger UI: {{baseUrl}}/api/docs/  (DEBUG mode only)
OpenAPI Schema: {{baseUrl}}/api/schema/

WebSocket endpoints:
  Notifications: ws://localhost:8000/ws/notifications/?token={{accessToken}}
  Chat room:     ws://localhost:8000/ws/chat/{{roomId}}/?token={{accessToken}}

request.description:
Create a new user account. Returns user + JWT token pair. Rate limited 10/min.

Response 201: `{ user: {...}, tokens: { access, refresh } }`

Authenticate and get JWT tokens.

Response 200: `{ access, refresh, user: { id, email, role } }`

exec: console.log('Tokens saved from Login, user:', json.user && json.user.email);

request.description:
Blacklist the refresh token, ending the session.

Response 200: `{ detail: 'Logged out successfully.' }`

Obtain a new access token using a valid refresh token.

Response 200: `{ access: 'eyJ...' }`

Returns the current user's profile.

Response 200: `{ id, email, full_name, phone, role, is_verified, created_at }`
Partial update of the current user. `full_name` and `phone` are writable; `role` and `email` are read-only.
Paginated list of venues. Requires authentication (staff or admin).

Create a venue. Admin only.

venue_type choices: airport | hotel | mall | restaurant | transport | government | other

{

  "contact_name": "Lost & Found Desk",

}

request.description:
Returns all venue type choices.

Response 200: `[{ value, label }]`
Retrieve a venue by its URL slug. Includes operating hours.
Partial update. Admin only.
Permanently delete a venue. Admin only. Response 204.

Get operating hours for a venue.

Response: `[{ day_of_week (0=Mon..6=Sun), opens_at, closes_at, is_closed }]`
Replace all operating hours for a venue. Provide all 7 days. Admin/staff only.

Set venue status to active. Admin only.

Response 200: `{ detail: 'Venue activated.' }`

Set venue status to inactive. Admin only.

Response 200: `{ detail: 'Venue deactivated.' }`

Paginated list of found items stored at venues. Any authenticated user can list.

Response 200: `{ results: [...], page: 1 }`

formdata.value: Found near Gate 5. Contains some cards, no cash.

formdata.description: Required - one or more item photos (repeat key for multiple)

request.description:
Upload a found item with one or more photos. Venue staff or admin only. Triggers async CLIP embedding via Celery. foundItemId is auto-saved on success.

Use the `images` key (repeat for multiple files) or the legacy single `image` key.

Response 201: Full MongoDB item document with `id` field.

Retrieve a single found item by its MongoDB ObjectId (stored in {{foundItemId}}).

Response 200: `{ id, title, category, status, images, image_url, venue_id, embedding_status }`

formdata.description: Required - CSV file. Required columns: title, description, category, found_at. Optional: color, brand, found_location.
Required for admins. Staff default to their assigned venue.

request.description:
Bulk-create found items from a CSV file. **Venue staff or admin only.** Images are not supported in bulk mode — embedding_status will be `skipped`.

CSV columns:
- `title` (required)
- `description` (required)
- `category` (required) — bag|phone|wallet|keys|clothing|document|electronics|jewelry|other
- `found_at` (required) — YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS
- `color` (optional)
- `brand` (optional)
- `found_location` (optional)

Response 201: `{ created, error_count, total_rows, errors: [{ row, errors }] }`

List the current user's lost items. Admin sees all.

Response 200: `{ results: [...], page: 1 }`

formdata.value: Lost my wallet at the airport. Contains driving license, 2 credit cards, and a family photo.

formdata.description: Optional - reference photo(s). Use `images` key (repeat for multiple) or legacy `image` key.

request.description:
Report a lost item. Any authenticated user. Image is optional — if provided, CLIP embedding is generated for AI matching. lostItemId is auto-saved.

Response 201: Full MongoDB item document.
Retrieve a lost item by its MongoDB ObjectId. Owners can only see their own items; admins can view all.

formdata.description: Optional - new image(s) to replace or add. Triggers new CLIP embedding.

request.description:
Partially update a lost item. **Owner only** (admins can update any). Writable fields: title, description, category, color, brand, lost_at, lost_location, status.

Valid status transitions: `searching` → `found` | `closed`.

If images are provided, CLIP embedding is re-generated.

Response 200: Updated item document.

Permanently delete a lost item. **Owner only** (admins can delete any).

Response 204: No content.

Get cached CLIP match results for a found item. Results populated asynchronously by Celery.

source: `cache` (Redis) or `live` (fresh Elasticsearch query)

Response 200: `{ results: [{ item_id, title, score, category }], source }`
Get cached CLIP match results for a lost item (returns matching found items).

Upload a photo and find visually similar items using CLIP image embeddings. Rate limited 30/min.

Response 200: `{ results: [{ item_id, title, score, category, venue_id }], total }`

Search items by natural-language description using CLIP text embeddings. Rate limited 30/min.

`category` is optional. `item_type`: found | lost.

Response 200: `{ results: [{ item_id, title, score, category }], total }`
List claims scoped by role. Admin: all. Venue staff: their venue only. Owner: their own claims only.

Submit a claim for an available found item. Owner only. Notifies venue staff via WebSocket. claimId is auto-saved.

`found_item_id`: 24-char MongoDB ObjectId. Item must be `status=available`.
`lost_item_id`: optional — links your lost item report to improve matching confidence.

Response 201: Full ClaimDetail object.
Retrieve a claim with full details: status history, pickup slot, claimant info, delivery info, and ID verification status.
Approve a pending/under_review claim. Venue staff or admin only. Notifies claimant via WebSocket. Status → approved.
Reject a claim with a reason. Venue staff or admin only. `rejection_reason` is required. Status → rejected.

Owner selects pickup slot after approval. Claimant only. `pickup_slot_id` required. Status → pickup_scheduled.

Use 'List Pickup Slots' to find available slots for the venue.
Owner requests courier delivery after approval. Claimant only. `delivery_address` required. Status → out_for_delivery.
Mark claim as completed — item handed over or dispatched. Venue staff or admin only. `delivery_tracking_id` is optional. Status → completed. Notifies claimant.
Cancel a claim. Claimant only. Cannot cancel completed or already-cancelled claims. Status → cancelled.

formdata.description: Required - photo of government-issued ID (passport, driving licence, etc.)

request.description:
Claimant uploads a photo of their government-issued ID for high-value item claims (phone, electronics, jewelry, wallet).

Response 200: `{ id_image_url: 'https://...' }`

Venue staff or admin marks the claimant's uploaded ID as verified after manual review.

Response 200: `{ id_verified: true }`

Admin only. List found items that have 2 or more competing active claims (pending, under_review, or approved).

Response 200: `{ results: [{ found_item_id, found_item: { title, category, image_url }, claims: [...] }], count }`

Admin only. Approve one winning claim and auto-reject all other active claims for the same found item.

Response 200: `{ winner_claim_id, rejected_count }`

List pickup slots. Non-staff users only see slots with remaining capacity.

Response 200: `{ count, results: [{ id, date, start_time, end_time, slots_remaining, is_available }] }`

Create a pickup slot. Venue staff or admin only. Staff don't need to specify `venue` — it defaults to their assigned venue. slotId is auto-saved.

Response 201: PickupSlot object.

Returns the 50 most recent notifications for the current user, newest first.

Response 200: `{ results: [{ id, type, title, message, data, is_read, created_at }], unread_count }`

Notification types: `match_found` | `claim_update` | `new_claim` (staff) | `system`

Mark notifications as read. Omit `ids` to mark all as read; pass a list of IDs to mark specific ones.

Response 204: No content.

List all chat rooms accessible to the current user.

- Regular users: only rooms tied to their own claims.
- Venue staff: rooms for their venue's claims.
- Admin: all rooms.

Each room includes a `found_item` snapshot fetched from MongoDB.

Response 200: `{ results: [{ id, claim_id, claim_status, claimant, venue_name, found_item, created_at }], count }`

Get or auto-create the chat room for a claim. Idempotent — calling it multiple times returns the same room. roomId is auto-saved on success.

Access: claimant, venue staff of that venue, or admin.

Response 200: `{ id, claim_id, created_at, message_count }`

query.description: Cursor: message ID for pagination (fetch messages older than this ID)

request.description:
Returns the 50 most recent messages in the room, oldest-first. Use `?before=<message_id>` for cursor-based pagination to load older messages.

Response 200: `{ room_id, results: [{ id, sender_id, sender_name, text, created_at }] }`

Returns the list of user IDs currently online in the room (tracked in Redis).

Response 200: `{ room_id, online_ids: [1, 2] }`

Admin only. Returns aggregate counts for the given lookback window.

Response 200:
```json
{
  "period_days": 30,
  "found_items": { "total", "new", "archived" },
  "lost_items":  { "total", "new" },
  "claims":      { "total", "new", "pending", "approved", "rejected", "completed" },
  "avg_resolution_hours": 4.2,
  "match_rate_pct": 68
}
```

Admin only. Returns per-day counts for found items, lost items, and claims — useful for time-series charts.

Response 200:
```json
{
  "period_days": 30,
  "found_items_per_day": [{ "date": "2026-10-01", "count": 5 }, ...],
  "lost_items_per_day":  [{ "date": "2026-10-01", "count": 3 }, ...],
  "claims_per_day":      [{ "date": "2026-10-01", "count": 2 }, ...]
}
```

Lightweight health check. Returns 200 if the server is up.

Response 200: `{ status: 'ok' }`
